title: Beyond the 956: Pete Edochie, Nollywood legend and star of 'Things Fall Apart,' dies at 79
excerpt: Pete Edochie, the Nigerian actor whose portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 television adaptation of Chinua Achebe's 'Things Fall Apart' made him one of Nollywood's most celebrated stars, died November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. He was 79.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Pete Edochie, the Nigerian actor whose commanding voice and unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart made him one of Nollywood's most celebrated stars, has died at 79.

Edochie died at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer, according to a statement issued by his family. His son, Leo Pete Edochie, announced the death on behalf of the family.

Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967 before turning to acting. His breakthrough came in 1987, when he played Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority's adaptation of Achebe's classic novel Things Fall Apart — a performance that brought him national and international attention, including an interview by the BBC.

Over a career spanning nearly six decades, Edochie became one of Nollywood's most recognizable figures, known for his deep voice, his delivery rich in traditional proverbs, and his powerful performances as rulers, elders and authority figures. His many film credits included Lionheart, the acclaimed Netflix film, and the popular Billionaires Club series. He was honored as a Member of the Order of the Niger (MON).

Edochie is survived by his wife, Barrister Josephine Edochie, his children — including actors Yul and Linc Edochie — and his siblings. Funeral arrangements will be announced by the family.

Sources: BBC News Africa; The Guardian Nigeria; family statement issued by Leo Pete Edochie.
